downloadPurpose: Private backend repo alpha risk handoff before real repo execution.

riskDomains.label: Repository control
riskDomains.note: Private visibility, PR-first branch discipline, and no direct main commits.

riskDomains.label: Secret handling
riskDomains.note: No live keys, .env files, billing secrets, tokens, or private certificates in the first repo.

riskDomains.label: Commercial privacy
riskDomains.note: Operational tracker examples must not expose values, agreements, LOA, invoices, or negotiation detail.

riskDomains.label: Tenant security
riskDomains.note: Company isolation, section access, denial audit, and commercial vault guards must exist before live data.

riskDomains.label: Data migration
riskDomains.note: Demo fixtures are allowed; real workbook import needs rollback, duplicate checks, and source trace.

riskDomains.label: CI and release
riskDomains.note: Workflow shells exist, but exact status check names appear only after the first run.

riskDomains.label: Scope control
riskDomains.note: Repo opening day approves shell and proof, not billing, production hosting, or live customer pilot.

riskDomains.label: Owner signoff
riskDomains.note: Founder, platform, backend, security, data, governance, and QA lanes must be explicit.

riskRegister.trigger: Repo created public or starter files uploaded before privacy is confirmed.
Any live token, .env file, key, or billing credential appears in the private repo.
Main receives direct files before develop branch, PR proof, and review discipline exist.
Required checks are configured before GitHub exposes the exact workflow status names.
Operational examples include value, agreement, LOA, invoice, billing, or negotiation fields.
Route shells skip company scope, section access, denied audit, or commercial vault guard.
Importer or seed work proceeds without dry-run, rollback, duplicate quarantine, or source trace.
First PR says checks pass but proof artifacts or placeholder notes are missing.
Payment keys, invoice workflow, or subscription logic moves before test-mode guardrails exist.
Team treats GitHub Pages prototype as production staging before real hosting, backups, and monitoring.
Reports, customer success, billing depth, or live import work enters the first backend shell PR.
No clear owner has authority to pause, approve, or reject the first backend PR.

triggerMatrix.response: Rotate, purge history, restart clean, and record the incident before continuing.
Stop file upload until the repository is private and visibility evidence is saved.
Remove restricted fields from examples and review redaction rules before PR continues.
Wait for the first GitHub Actions run before applying branch protection.
Do not review PR until issue, labels, milestone, proof lane, and owner are attached.
Add rollback thinking even for shell initialization work.
Accept only when the PR clearly names why command output is placeholder and what will replace it.
Move non-shell work into later M1/M2 issues before first PR approval.

mitigationPlan.action: Owner confirms private visibility before any starter file, issue, or evidence packet moves.
Run manual scan for .env, tokens, keys, billing credentials, certificates, and customer files.
Keep operational payloads free of restricted commercial fields.
Generated issues provide labels, milestones, owners, and proof lanes for traceability.
Capture exact status check names from the first workflow run, then protect main.
First PR includes release note, rollback note, evidence files, and owner signoffs.
Use generated demo fixtures only until import rollback and tenant guards are implemented.
Block customer data until tenant access, audit, redaction, backup, billing test mode, and restore checks pass.

ownerActions.action: Confirms scope cutline, no-live-data rule, and go/hold/no-go decision.
Creates repo, opens branch, copies files, imports taxonomy, and captures workflow names.
Owns API boot, route registry, middleware order, proof commands, and PR scope.
Owns secrets, tenant isolation, access decisions, commercial redaction, and denial audit.
Owns fixtures, seed order, migration rollback, duplicate quarantine, and source trace.
Owns proof packet, release gate, branch protection evidence, and signoff checklist.

decisionRules.rule: Private repo, no secrets, issue trace, proof packet, rollback note, and owner signoffs are ready.
Branch protection is delayed until check names are visible, and this is documented.
Repo can be created, but issue import waits for taxonomy or owner confirmation.
First PR lacks proof outputs, placeholder explanation, or release-gate summary.
Branch protection settings are guessed before first workflow run.
Repository is public, live secrets are committed, or customer data enters the repo.
Commercial fields leak into operational examples or tracker payloads.
Tenant, access, redaction, or audit guardrails are removed from starter scope.

monitoringSignals.note: Visibility proof must be captured before files move.
Develop branch opens first PR to main; no direct main commits.
Any secret-like material triggers stop, rotation, and cleanup.
Install, quality, route, auth, redaction, audit, and release proof are addressed.
Check names are mapped after first run, then branch rules are applied.
M0/M1 opening order keeps foundation and security first.

residualRisks.note: No live staging exists until hosting, database, secrets, monitoring, and backups are implemented.
Membership is modeled; checkout and invoices remain future backend work.
Workbook parser and rollback runner are not implemented until backend routes exist.
Feedback, training, and support workflows still need database persistence.
No scale testing exists until API and database are real.
Formal legal/security review waits until production stack and data residency are chosen.

acceptanceChecks.note: Eight domains cover repo, secret, commercial, tenant, data, CI, scope, and owner risk.
Twelve alpha risks have severity, trigger, and mitigation language.
Eight triggers define stop, hold, and watch behavior.
Eight mitigations connect timing to exact controls.
Eight rules define go, conditional go, hold, and no-go.
Six accepted or watched risks remain transparent.
v127 can turn the runbook into evidence files, proof screenshots, logs, and PR notes.

handoff: v126 turns the repo decision into an alpha risk register before real backend execution begins.
The register makes the controlled-go decision safer by naming hard stops, hold points, owner lanes, mitigations, residual risks, and monitoring signals.
The biggest risks remain repo visibility, secrets, commercial leakage, tenant isolation, branch discipline, and treating prototype planning as live SaaS readiness.
v127 can now produce the opening-day evidence pack: proof files, screenshots, logs, PR notes, workflow check names, and branch-protection evidence.
